description: NovaPulse is a multidisciplinary team passionate about cybersecurity, software development, AI, and space exploration. We aim to transform complex astronaut health data into intelligent, secure, and actionable insights, helping astronauts monitor their well-being, detect anomalies early, and make informed decisions during long-duration space missions.
summary:
NovaPulse is an offline-first, on-board health assistant for astronauts on deep-space missions, where live contact with ground medical teams is not possible. It learns each astronaut's personal baseline instead of using population averages, and scores five health domains from 0 to 100: cardiovascular, immune, bone and muscle, behavioral, and radiation.

Six machine learning models, trained offline on public NASA and wearable datasets (NASA Flight Crew Physiological Data, LifeSnaps, MMASH), estimate overall health, fatigue, cardiovascular and sleep risk, mission status, and anomalies. They run locally, with no internet connection.

Every alert is explained with its evidence, likely cause, confidence level and ranked actions, including escalation to the flight surgeon. Our prototype simulates a 200-day mission with three crew members, a time-lapse scrubber and scenario buttons, such as a solar radiation storm, so judges can watch scores and alerts react live.

NovaPulse supports decisions rather than replacing medical professionals, helping crews detect risks early, far from Earth.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

NovaPulse monitors the health of astronauts on long deep-space missions, where real-time contact with Earth is limited. For each crew member it learns a personal baseline from daily telemetry (heart rate, HRV, blood pressure, SpO2, temperature, sleep, stress, fatigue, radiation dose, cabin CO2) and scores five health domains from 0 to 100: cardiovascular, immune, bone and muscle, behavioral, and radiation. When something drifts from the baseline, NovaPulse raises an alert that explains itself: the evidence, the likely cause, a confidence level and ranked actions, with escalation to the flight surgeon when needed.

HOW IT WORKS

A Python simulator generates a reproducible 200-day mission for three astronauts (Nadia, Leo and Aiko). A FastAPI backend serves the data, validates every reading against physiological bounds and exposes a REST API. Six scikit-learn models, trained offline on 35 input features and loaded locally, predict overall health score, fatigue risk, cardiovascular risk, sleep risk, mission status and anomalies (Random Forests plus an Isolation Forest). The React dashboard combines these predictions with z-score analysis against each astronaut's baseline, a 72-hour trend estimate, a time-lapse scrubber, and scenario buttons (solar radiation storm, infection, sleep disruption, exercise decline, isolation, cabin CO2 rise) that replay the mission live.

DATA

The models use public datasets: LifeSnaps (Fitbit wearable data), MMASH (PhysioNet, 22 adults monitored for 24 hours) and NASA physiological data. We cleaned, merged and standardized them into one unified format, with one row per subject per day. Space-weather events such as flares and CME come from NASA DONKI, with a cached snapshot as fallback when there is no connection.

TOOLS

React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Zustand, Recharts, React Router and Dexie for the interface. Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLite, scikit-learn, pandas and NumPy for the backend and AI. ECDSA P-256 signatures and SHA-256 hashing via the cryptography library. Tests with pytest and the Node test runner. Deployed on Microsoft Azure App Service.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

NovaPulse gives early warnings before a small drift becomes an emergency, and it explains every alert so crews can trust it. Inference uses local model files and needs no internet connection. It is a decision-support tool, not a replacement for medical professionals. The same approach could also support other isolated environments, such as polar stations or remote expeditions.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It combines personal baselines, machine learning and plain-language explanations in one assistant. Ground reports are signed with ECDSA and delayed to simulate communication latency. The audit log is tamper-evident through a SHA-256 hash chain. Low confidence is shown openly instead of hidden. Scenario buttons let judges trigger events and watch scores and alerts react.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Offline operation and communication delay, safety (decision support only), explainability, data integrity and traceability, strict physiological validation, and reproducibility through seeded simulation. We also took into account that public datasets and simulated telemetry stand in for real astronaut data, and that missing sensors, such as EEG, use simulated values.
